target.title: fix(core): use UTF-16-safe truncation for chat display, ACP stream relay, and native hook relay
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Three truncation helpers in core used raw `String.prototype.slice`, which can split supplementary-plane characters (emoji, CJK extension B+, etc.) into lone surrogate halves when the cutoff lands between a high/low surrogate pair. This produces malformed UTF-16 in user-visible display text — the same class of bug as #99566, which fixed the exec approval command display path.

| Site | Cap | Risk |
|------|-----|------|
| `chat-display-projection.ts` — `truncateChatHistoryText` | 8 KiB | Very high — core display pipeline, every chat message goes through it, messages frequently contain emoji |
| `acp-spawn-parent-stream.ts` — `truncate()` | 220 chars | High — short boundary, agent streaming output often contains emoji; collision probability much higher than #99566's 16 KiB cap |
| `native-hook-relay.ts` — `truncateText()` | 80/240/700 chars | Medium-high — approval UI (title, description, command key), same exec-approval-command-display security decision surface as #99566 |

## Summary

- Switch all three truncation helpers to the shared `truncateUtf16Safe` from `src/shared/utf16-slice.js` (the same helper introduced in #99566).
- Add regression tests: construct a string with an emoji whose surrogate pair crosses the truncation boundary, verify no lone surrogate in output.
- The fix is mechanical: each site changes one `value.slice(0, N)` call to `truncateUtf16Safe(value, N)` and adds one import.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/chat-display-projection.test.ts` — 4 files, 12 tests passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/acp-spawn-parent-stream.test.ts` — 1 file, 35 tests passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay.test.ts` — 1 file, 77 tests passed
- `pnpm exec oxlint` on all 6 changed files — 0 warnings
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1` on all 6 changed files — clean
- Confirmed via runtime: the acp-spawn-parent-stream test places `😀` at positions 218-219 so old `slice(0, 219)` produces a lone high surrogate (0xD83D); `truncateUtf16Safe` correctly backs off to 218

## Risk

Low. This only changes the truncation boundary to back off from split surrogate pairs. It does not change truncation caps, markers, redaction logic, or any product behavior. The shared helper is dependency-free (no `node:` imports) and already used in production in `exec-approval-command-display.ts` since #99566 landed.
